description: Figure 2 illustrates the training loss as a function of training steps for six different model configurations, all trained on a dataset of 20 million samples. The x-axis, labeled “Step,” is presented on a linear scale ranging from 0K to 440K, with major tick marks at intervals of 20K up to 80K, followed by 420K and 440K, suggesting a zoomed-in or non-uniform display for later steps. The y-axis, labeled “Train Loss,” spans from 0.0 to 0.85 in linear increments, with visible gridlines at 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, and 0.8. Six distinct lines represent different model types and sizes: ChemBART Small 20M (red, solid), ChemBART Medium 20M (blue, solid), ChemBERTa Small 20M (green, solid), ChemBERTa Medium 20M (orange, solid), ChemLLaMA Small 20M (purple, solid), and ChemLLaMA Medium 20M (brown, solid). All lines begin near 0.85 at 0K steps and exhibit a sharp decline in the first 20K steps, after which the rate of decrease slows. By 80K steps, all models have converged to train loss values below 0.2. In the zoomed-in inset showing steps from 420K to 440K, all lines remain relatively flat and close to each other, hovering just above 0.0, indicating convergence. The legend is positioned in the upper right corner, clearly associating each color with its corresponding model configuration.
